# core/bytes.bastio

<!-- Generated by tests/libref.py from core/bytes.bastio: edit the source, then run tests/libref.py --write. -->

Comparing, searching, slicing and hashing byte strings.

Byte strings are compared and searched in place: functions take positions
or a `Span` (bytes `start..end`) instead of copies, and copy only when
asked (`bytes_slice`). A scan for one byte returns the length of the string
when the byte is absent, so a scan loop needs no `match`.

What is proved: each comparison returns exactly the relation its spec fn
names (`bytes_equal`, `bytes_equal_str`, `bytes_same_at`); a search result
is a real occurrence, and every byte a search skipped differs; copies and
writes change only the bytes they name. Not proved: that `bytes_find`
finds the first occurrence, or any. A precondition such as
`to <= blen(b)` is proved at each call: `bytes_slice(b, 2, 9)` on five
bytes is rejected at compile time.

`import "core/bytes.bastio";` also loads [core/option.bastio](core-option.md).

| Function | |
| --- | --- |
| [`bytes_eq`](#bytes_eq) | `a` and `b` hold the same bytes. |
| [`bytes_eq_str`](#bytes_eq_str) | `a` holds exactly the bytes of the literal `s`. |
| [`bytes_span_eq_str`](#bytes_span_eq_str) | Bytes `from..to` of `a` are the bytes of `s`. |
| [`bytes_starts_with`](#bytes_starts_with) | `a` begins with `p`. |
| [`bytes_ends_with`](#bytes_ends_with) | `a` ends with `p`. |
| [`bytes_cmp`](#bytes_cmp) | Lexicographic order. |
| [`bytes_find_byte`](#bytes_find_byte) | The first index at or after `from` holding `c`, or `blen(b)` if there is none. |
| [`bytes_rfind_byte`](#bytes_rfind_byte) | The last index below `to` holding `c`, if any. |
| [`bytes_find`](#bytes_find) | The first index at or after `from` where `needle` occurs in `hay`, if any. |
| [`bytes_slice`](#bytes_slice) | A copy of bytes `from..to` of `b`. |
| [`bytes_concat`](#bytes_concat) | A new byte string holding `a` followed by `b`. |
| [`bytes_copy_into`](#bytes_copy_into) | Copies `src` into `dst` at `at`, leaving the other bytes of `dst` alone. |
| [`bytes_span_eq`](#bytes_span_eq) | Bytes `a[i..i+n]` and `b[j..j+n]` are equal (`a` and `b` may be the same string). |
| [`bytes_copy_span`](#bytes_copy_span) | Copies `src[from..to]` into `dst` at `at`, leaving the other bytes of `dst` alone. |
| [`bytes_put_byte`](#bytes_put_byte) | Writes `c` at `at` if it fits. |
| [`bytes_put_str`](#bytes_put_str) | Writes the literal `s` at `at`, as much of it as fits. |
| [`is_space`](#is_space) | Space, tab, newline or carriage return. |
| [`bytes_trim`](#bytes_trim) | `s` without the white space (`is_space`) at either end. |
| [`bytes_split`](#bytes_split) | The pieces of `b` between occurrences of `sep`, in order. |
| [`bytes_hash`](#bytes_hash) | The 64-bit FNV-1a hash of `b`. |
| [`bytes_vec_free`](#bytes_vec_free) | Frees a vector of byte strings and every string in it. |

Every example below is built, verified and run by `tests/run.sh`. An `assert` in one is proved at compile time from the contracts above it.

## Functions

### `bytes_eq`

```bastio
fn bytes_eq(a: &Bytes, b: &Bytes) -> bool
  ensures result == bytes_equal(a, b)
```

`a` and `b` hold the same bytes.

Example:

```bastio
let a = bfrom("abc");
let b = bfrom("abc");
let c = bfrom("abd");
let same = bytes_eq(a, b);
let differ = bytes_eq(a, c);
bfree(a);
bfree(b);
bfree(c);
if !same || differ { return 1; }
```

### `bytes_eq_str`

```bastio
fn bytes_eq_str(a: &Bytes, s: Str) -> bool
  ensures result == bytes_equal_str(a, s)
```

`a` holds exactly the bytes of the literal `s`.

Example:

```bastio
let cmd = bfrom("exit");
if !bytes_eq_str(cmd, "exit") {
  bfree(cmd);
  return 1;
}
assert blen(cmd) == 4;   // known from the contract: equal means the same length
bfree(cmd);
```

### `bytes_span_eq_str`

```bastio
fn bytes_span_eq_str(a: &Bytes, from: u64, to: u64, s: Str) -> bool
  requires from <= to && to <= blen(a)
  ensures result == (to - from == slen(s) && (forall k: u64 :: k < slen(s) ==> bget(a, from + k) == sget(s, k)))
```

Bytes `from..to` of `a` are the bytes of `s`.

Example:

```bastio
let line = bfrom("GET /index.html");
let get = bytes_span_eq_str(line, 0, 3, "GET");   // the method is bytes 0..3
let put = bytes_span_eq_str(line, 0, 3, "PUT");
bfree(line);
if !get || put { return 1; }
```

### `bytes_starts_with`

```bastio
fn bytes_starts_with(a: &Bytes, p: &Bytes) -> bool
  ensures result == (blen(p) <= blen(a) && bytes_same_at(a, 0, p, 0, blen(p)))
```

`a` begins with `p`.

Example:

```bastio
let path = bfrom("/proc/1/status");
let pre = bfrom("/proc/");
let suf = bfrom("/status");
let ok = bytes_starts_with(path, pre) && bytes_ends_with(path, suf) && !bytes_starts_with(pre, path);
bfree(path);
bfree(pre);
bfree(suf);
if !ok { return 1; }
```

### `bytes_ends_with`

```bastio
fn bytes_ends_with(a: &Bytes, p: &Bytes) -> bool
  ensures result == (blen(p) <= blen(a) && bytes_same_at(a, blen(a) - blen(p), p, 0, blen(p)))
```

`a` ends with `p`.

### `bytes_cmp`

```bastio
fn bytes_cmp(a: &Bytes, b: &Bytes) -> i8
  ensures result == -1 || result == 0 || result == 1
  ensures (result == 0) == bytes_equal(a, b)
```

Lexicographic order: -1 if `a` sorts before `b`, 0 if they are equal,
1 if after. A proper prefix sorts first.

Example:

```bastio
let a = bfrom("apple");
let b = bfrom("apricot");
let c = bfrom("app");
let r1 = bytes_cmp(a, b);   // 'p' sorts before 'r'
let r2 = bytes_cmp(c, a);   // a proper prefix sorts first
let r3 = bytes_cmp(b, b);
bfree(a);
bfree(b);
bfree(c);
if r1 != -1 || r2 != -1 || r3 != 0 { return 1; }
```

### `bytes_find_byte`

```bastio
fn bytes_find_byte(b: &Bytes, c: u8, from: u64) -> u64
  requires from <= blen(b)
  ensures from <= result && result <= blen(b)
  ensures result < blen(b) ==> bget(b, result) == c
  ensures forall k: u64 :: from <= k && k < result ==> bget(b, k) != c
```

The first index at or after `from` holding `c`, or `blen(b)` if there is none.

Example:

```bastio
let line = bfrom("name=bastio");
let eq = bytes_find_byte(line, 61, 0);     // '='
let hash = bytes_find_byte(line, 35, 0);   // no '#': the length
let n = blen(line);
bfree(line);
if eq != 4 || hash != n { return 1; }
```

### `bytes_rfind_byte`

```bastio
fn bytes_rfind_byte(b: &Bytes, c: u8, to: u64) -> Option[u64]
  requires to <= blen(b)
  ensures result is Option::Some ==> result.Some < to && bget(b, result.Some) == c
  ensures result is Option::Some ==> (forall k: u64 :: result.Some < k && k < to ==> bget(b, k) != c)
  ensures result is Option::None ==> (forall k: u64 :: k < to ==> bget(b, k) != c)
```

The last index below `to` holding `c`, if any: where the last `/` of a
path is, say.

Example:

```bastio
let path = bfrom("/usr/lib/libc.so");
let mut base = 0;
match bytes_rfind_byte(path, 47, blen(path)) {   // the last '/'
  Option::Some(i) => { base = i + 1; },
  Option::None => {},
}
let ok = bytes_span_eq_str(path, base, blen(path), "libc.so");
let none = bytes_rfind_byte(path, 47, 0);   // nothing below 0
bfree(path);
if !ok || none is Option::Some { return 1; }
```

### `bytes_find`

```bastio
fn bytes_find(hay: &Bytes, needle: &Bytes, from: u64) -> Option[u64]
  requires from <= blen(hay)
  ensures result is Option::Some ==> from <= result.Some && result.Some + blen(needle) <= blen(hay)
  ensures result is Option::Some ==> bytes_same_at(hay, result.Some, needle, 0, blen(needle))
```

The first index at or after `from` where `needle` occurs in `hay`, if
any. Proved: a `Some` is a real occurrence. Not proved: that it is the
first, or that `None` means there is none (the statement needs a
quantifier Z3 cannot instantiate in every program).

Example:

```bastio
let hay = bfrom("a needle in a haystack");
let needle = bfrom("needle");
let mut at = 0;
match bytes_find(hay, needle, 0) {
  Option::Some(i) => {
    // The contract says the needle is there, so this slice needs no check.
    let found = bytes_slice(hay, i, i + blen(needle));
    if !bytes_eq(found, needle) { at = 99; } else { at = i; }
    bfree(found);
  },
  Option::None => { at = 99; },
}
bfree(hay);
bfree(needle);
if at != 2 { return 1; }
```

### `bytes_slice`

```bastio
fn bytes_slice(b: &Bytes, from: u64, to: u64) -> Bytes
  requires from <= to && to <= blen(b)
  ensures blen(result) == to - from && bytes_same_at(result, 0, b, from, to - from)
```

A copy of bytes `from..to` of `b`.

Example:

```bastio
let b = bfrom("hello, world");
let w = bytes_slice(b, 7, 12);
assert blen(w) == 5;
let ok = bytes_eq_str(w, "world");
bfree(w);
bfree(b);
if !ok { return 1; }
```

### `bytes_concat`

```bastio
fn bytes_concat(a: &Bytes, b: &Bytes) -> Bytes
  requires blen(a) + blen(b) <= 1152921504606846976
  ensures blen(result) == blen(a) + blen(b)
  ensures bytes_same_at(result, 0, a, 0, blen(a)) && bytes_same_at(result, blen(a), b, 0, blen(b))
```

A new byte string holding `a` followed by `b`. Every `Bytes` is known to
be at most 2^60 long, but two together are not (nothing bounds the memory
of all live values at once), so for strings of unknown length build a
text instead (core/text.bastio).

Example:

```bastio
let a = bfrom("foo");
let b = bfrom("bar");
let ab = bytes_concat(a, b);
assert blen(ab) == 6;
let ok = bytes_eq_str(ab, "foobar");
bfree(ab);
bfree(a);
bfree(b);
if !ok { return 1; }
```

### `bytes_copy_into`

```bastio
fn bytes_copy_into(dst: &mut Bytes, at: u64, src: &Bytes)
  requires at + blen(src) <= blen(dst)
  ensures blen(dst) == blen(old(dst))
  ensures bytes_same_at(dst, at, src, 0, blen(src))
  ensures forall k: u64 :: k < blen(dst) && (k < at || k >= at + blen(src)) ==> bget(dst, k) == bget(old(dst), k)
```

Copies `src` into `dst` at `at`, leaving the other bytes of `dst` alone.

Example:

```bastio
let mut buf = bfrom("........");
let src = bfrom("abc");
bytes_copy_into(&mut buf, 2, src);
let ok = bytes_eq_str(buf, "..abc...");
bfree(buf);
bfree(src);
if !ok { return 1; }
```

### `bytes_span_eq`

```bastio
fn bytes_span_eq(a: &Bytes, i: u64, b: &Bytes, j: u64, n: u64) -> bool
  requires i <= blen(a) && n <= blen(a) - i && j <= blen(b) && n <= blen(b) - j
  ensures result == (forall p: u64 :: i <= p && p < i + n ==> bget(a, p) == bget(b, p - i + j))
```

Bytes `a[i..i+n]` and `b[j..j+n]` are equal (`a` and `b` may be the
same string). The contract counts positions in `a` (`p` for `a`, the
same distance into `b`): stated with one offset into each string, the
proof needs Z3's model-based instantiation, which a program whose
struct invariants bring in `vcount`'s lemmas does not get.

Example:

```bastio
let a = bfrom("xxabcxx");
let b = bfrom("abc");
let ok = bytes_span_eq(a, 2, b, 0, 3) && !bytes_span_eq(a, 0, b, 0, 3) && bytes_span_eq(a, 0, a, 5, 2);
bfree(a);
bfree(b);
if !ok { return 1; }
```

### `bytes_copy_span`

```bastio
fn bytes_copy_span(dst: &mut Bytes, at: u64, src: &Bytes, from: u64, to: u64)
  requires from <= to && to <= blen(src) && at <= blen(dst) && to - from <= blen(dst) - at
  ensures blen(dst) == blen(old(dst))
  ensures bytes_same_at(dst, at, src, from, to - from)
  ensures forall k: u64 :: k < blen(dst) && (k < at || k >= at + (to - from)) ==> bget(dst, k) == bget(old(dst), k)
```

Copies `src[from..to]` into `dst` at `at`, leaving the other bytes of
`dst` alone. One `bcopy`: no per-byte loop.

Example:

```bastio
let mut dst = bfrom("....");
let src = bfrom("0123456789");
bytes_copy_span(&mut dst, 0, src, 3, 7);
let ok = bytes_eq_str(dst, "3456");
bfree(dst);
bfree(src);
if !ok { return 1; }
```

### `bytes_put_byte`

```bastio
fn bytes_put_byte(dst: &mut Bytes, at: u64, c: u8) -> u64
  requires at <= blen(dst)
  ensures blen(dst) == blen(old(dst)) && at <= result && result <= blen(dst)
  ensures at < blen(dst) ==> result == at + 1 && bget(dst, at) == c
  ensures forall k: u64 :: k < blen(dst) && k != at ==> bget(dst, k) == bget(old(dst), k)
```

Writes `c` at `at` if it fits. Returns the position after it, or `at`
when `dst` is full there: a writer into a fixed buffer chains these and
drops what does not fit.

Example:

```bastio
// A reply built in a fixed 8-byte buffer: what does not fit is dropped.
let mut o = balloc(8);
let mut at = bytes_put_str(&mut o, 0, "pid:");
at = bytes_put_byte(&mut o, at, 32);
at = bytes_put_str(&mut o, at, "1234567");   // only "123" fits
assert at <= 8;
let ok = at == 8 && bytes_eq_str(o, "pid: 123");
bfree(o);
if !ok { return 1; }
```

### `bytes_put_str`

```bastio
fn bytes_put_str(dst: &mut Bytes, at: u64, s: Str) -> u64
  requires at <= blen(dst)
  ensures blen(dst) == blen(old(dst)) && at <= result && result <= blen(dst)
  ensures slen(s) <= blen(dst) - at ==> result == at + slen(s)
  ensures forall k: u64 :: at <= k && k < result ==> bget(dst, k) == sget(s, k - at)
  ensures forall k: u64 :: k < blen(dst) && (k < at || k >= result) ==> bget(dst, k) == bget(old(dst), k)
```

Writes the literal `s` at `at`, as much of it as fits. Returns the
position after what was written.

### `is_space`

```bastio
fn is_space(c: u8) -> bool
  ensures result == (c == 32 || c == 9 || c == 10 || c == 13)
```

Space, tab, newline or carriage return.

### `bytes_trim`

```bastio
fn bytes_trim(b: &Bytes, s: Span) -> Span
  requires span_in(s, b)
  ensures s.start <= result.start && result.start <= result.end && result.end <= s.end
  ensures forall k: u64 :: s.start <= k && k < result.start ==> is_space_spec(bget(b, k))
  ensures forall k: u64 :: result.end <= k && k < s.end ==> is_space_spec(bget(b, k))
  ensures result.start < result.end ==> !is_space_spec(bget(b, result.start)) && !is_space_spec(bget(b, result.end - 1))
```

`s` without the white space (`is_space`) at either end.

Example:

```bastio
let b = bfrom("  key = value \n");
let s = bytes_trim(b, Span { start: 0, end: blen(b) });
// The result is a span of `b`, so it can be compared without a check.
let ok = bytes_span_eq_str(b, s.start, s.end, "key = value") && is_space(9) && !is_space(65);
bfree(b);
if !ok { return 1; }
```

### `bytes_split`

```bastio
fn bytes_split(b: &Bytes, sep: u8) -> Vec[Span]
  ensures vlen(result) >= 1
  ensures forall i: u64 :: i < vlen(result) ==> span_in(vget(result, i), b)
```

The pieces of `b` between occurrences of `sep`, in order. There is one
more piece than there are separators, so an empty `b` gives one empty span.

Example:

```bastio
let b = bfrom("a,bc,,d");
let parts = bytes_split(b, 44);   // ','
let mut ok = vec_len(parts) == 4;
if ok {
  // Every piece is a span of `b`, so reading it needs no check.
  let p = vec_get(parts, 1);
  let q = vec_get(parts, 2);
  ok = bytes_span_eq_str(b, p.start, p.end, "bc") && q.start == q.end;
}
vec_free(parts);
bfree(b);
if !ok { return 1; }
```

### `bytes_hash`

```bastio
fn bytes_hash(b: &Bytes) -> u64
```

The 64-bit FNV-1a hash of `b`.

Example:

```bastio
let a = bfrom("key");
let b = bfrom("key");
let e = balloc(0);
let ok = bytes_hash(a) == bytes_hash(b) && bytes_hash(e) == 14695981039346656037;
bfree(a);
bfree(b);
bfree(e);
if !ok { return 1; }
```

### `bytes_vec_free`

```bastio
fn bytes_vec_free(v: Vec[Bytes])
```

Frees a vector of byte strings and every string in it.

Example:

```bastio
let mut argv = vec_new[Bytes]();
vec_push(&mut argv, bfrom("echo"));
vec_push(&mut argv, bfrom("hi"));
bytes_vec_free(argv);
```

## Specification functions

### `bytes_same_at`

```bastio
spec fn bytes_same_at(a: &Bytes, i: u64, b: &Bytes, j: u64, n: u64) -> bool {
  forall k: u64 :: k < n ==> bget(a, i + k) == bget(b, j + k)
}
```

Bytes `a[i..i+n]` and `b[j..j+n]` are equal.

### `bytes_equal`

```bastio
spec fn bytes_equal(a: &Bytes, b: &Bytes) -> bool {
  blen(a) == blen(b) && bytes_same_at(a, 0, b, 0, blen(a))
}
```

`a` and `b` hold the same bytes.

### `bytes_equal_str`

```bastio
spec fn bytes_equal_str(a: &Bytes, s: Str) -> bool {
  blen(a) == slen(s) && (forall k: u64 :: k < blen(a) ==> bget(a, k) == sget(s, k))
}
```

`a` holds exactly the bytes of the literal `s`.

### `span_in`

```bastio
spec fn span_in(s: Span, b: &Bytes) -> bool {
  s.start <= s.end && s.end <= blen(b)
}
```

`s` is a span of `b`.

### `is_space_spec`

```bastio
spec fn is_space_spec(c: u8) -> bool {
  c == 32 || c == 9 || c == 10 || c == 13
}
```

Space, tab, newline or carriage return.
